params.body:
## What

Dutch text addressed its reader in two registers: 66 lines in 21 language files said "u" or "uw", the rest said "je". This converts them all to "je" and "jouw", rewritten as sentences and not by search and replace ("Bent u zeker dat u ..." becomes "Ben je zeker dat je ...", "Gelieve uw gegevens na te kijken" becomes "Kijk je gegevens na", "U wordt gecontacteerd" becomes "We contacteren je", "Prijzen blijven altijd van u" becomes "van jou").

- `resources/lang/nl`: access, anomaly, api, carDna, carVWE, chatbot, dealer, export, features, global, lead, manual_documents, ownstock, setting, settings, user, vehicle, vote, warranty, website, worklist.
- Hardcoded Dutch: the proposal modal and its refusal message, the public proposal page, its expired page and its mail.
- Business rules: the quotes in S2-4.3, S4-2.18, B1-5.4, B1-5.5, P1-3.3 and P3-16.21 follow the new text; new rule P2-2.18 states the tone of address.
- Knowledge base: one orphaned fragment ("u ingevuld.") removed from a manual. LYRA's persona already says "je".

## Left formal, on purpose

- Five keys in `export.php` that are printed documents handed to the buyer of a car with the take-over agreement (`belangrijke_opmerkingen_opsomming`, `bijlage_formal`, `formaliteiten_inleiding`, `formaliteiten_nieuw_voertuig`, `formalities`). They are on the allowlist of the new test, each with its reason.
- The platform terms quoted in `docs/kennisbank/faq.md` (contract text).
- `docs/kennisbank/verkoopstechniek/`: the "u" there is inside example sentences a salesperson says to a customer; the text that speaks to the dealer already says "je". Changing the quotes would change the advice.
- `resources/lang/nl/email.php` and `transport.php`, and the transport mail blades: the transport-mail rewrite owns them. They sit on a temporary list in the test, to be removed there.
- Findings and source notes under `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen` and `bronnen`: they record what the screen said on that day, and a Car-Pass error message.
- French, German, English and Spanish are unchanged.

## "Het kantoor"

The platform calls itself "we". Outside `email.php` and `transport.php` (all languages) no text a dealer reads says "het kantoor", "le bureau", "the office" or "das Büro"; the remaining hits in `app/` are English code comments. The lint below now refuses the Dutch word, so the transport-mail rewrite is the only place left to convert.

## Translations in the database

Nothing in the database overrides these files. `language_lines` has no reader left: the Spatie loader is gone from `config/app.php` and `composer.json`, and the only code that names the table is the one-off export command and two table lists for copying databases. `resources/lang/nl/lbl.php` still reads the `labels` table, but no code requests a `lbl.` key, the helper that did (`app/Http/Hooks/trans.php`) is never loaded, and the file selects a column (`name_1`) the table no longer has. So no migration is needed, and none is included.

## Test

`DutchSaysJeNotUTest` reads every Dutch language line (and `nl.json`) and fails on a word-bounded "u", "uw" or "kantoor" outside the allowlists; a third test fails when an allowlisted key no longer exists or no longer needs its exception.
params.title: Dutch says je, not u: one tone of address in every text a dealer reads
